newsitem.title: GREECE: Banks buy $800 mln at Greek fix, boosting $/dr.
newsitem.headline: Banks buy $800 mln at Greek fix, boosting $/dr.

text.p: Banks bought $800 million, the amount they had borrowed to buy into a maturing state $-linked bond, at the Greek central bank's fixing, a high-level central bank official told Reuters. This drove the dollar/drachma up to 246.920 from Wednesday's 245.560.

"Banks bought $800 million for drachmas at the fixing which corresponds to a maturing $-linked bond issued by the Hellenic Republic," said a high-level central bank official. "This pulled $/drachma up and therefore the crosses."
The much watched ecu/drachma exchange rate ended at 305.400 on Thursday from Wednesday's 304.910, up 0.54 percent year-to-date.

The Bank of Greece has pre-announced that it wants ecu/drachma to remain broadly stable in 1996. The market has interpreted the announcement as meaning that the drachma will depreciate by about one percent against the ecu in 1996.
The central bank has yet to announce its foreign exchange policy for 1997.
"The markets are calm and there are no speculative moves," the central bank official said.

London-based dealers told Reuters that a combination of steady overnight intervention rates by the central bank and aggressive slashing of interest rates of state securities by the finance ministry would lead to forex outflows.

The Bank of Greece has kept its overnight bid and offer intervention rates unchanged at 12.40 percent and 13.40 percent respectively in the last couple of months but the treasury has cut its key 12-month T-bill rate to 11.50 percent from 12.70 percent in September.
Many banks fund their purchases of Greek treasuries in the interbank market.
